previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis and a long-standing suprapubic catheter, was admitted due to leakage around the catheter site and associated fatigue. He had no fever or pain, but urinalysis showed elevated white blood cells, prompting initial empiric antibiotics. Urology exchanged the obstructed catheter in the emergency department. Given his lack of infection symptoms and a urine culture consistent with contamination, antibiotics were discontinued. He was monitored for 24 hours off treatment, remained stable, and was discharged home after two days. The final assessment was mechanical obstruction of the suprapubic catheter with chronic bacterial colonization, not active infection.
problems: Other mechanical complication of genitourinary device, implant, and graft
Urinary catheterization as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure
Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
Carrier or suspected carrier of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ with MS ___ neurogenic bladder s/p chronic 
indwelling suprapubic tube with history of multiple UTIs who 
presents with lethargy and bloody urine.  

# Complicated UTI: Patient presents with fatigue and bloody 
urine found to have grossly positive UA (albeit with 10Epis) and 
leukocytosis to WBC 21. On exam, no flank pain to suggest 
ascending infection/pyelo. Given neurogenic bladder and 
suprapubic catheter, treated for complicated UTI. Review of 
prior urine cultures show that patient has recently ___ grown 
Providencia, Proteus mirabalis, Pseudomonas (R-FQs), E.coli, and 
Vanc-sensitive Enteroccocus. Patient was adminsitered 
ceftriaxone in the ED, broadened to Vanc/Cefepime on admission. 
Though was feeling better, his WBC was further increased to 25 
on HD2. Given his history of Providencia UTI, which does have an 
inducible beta-lactamase gene (ampC), cefepime was changed to 
Meropenem. His first urine culture unfortunately returned 
contaminated with fecal flora and his repeat culture was 
sterilized by his antibiotics. Vancomycin was discontinued and 
meropenem was changed to cefepime to narrow coverage and 
simplify regimen. WBC continued to trend down and patient had no 
fevers or new symptoms on this regimen. Midline was placed in 
preparation for discharge with home IV antibiotics. 
Unfortunately, the patient has had issues with reliable 
administration of home antibiotics in the past and his case was 
rejected by the home infusion company. He remained in the 
hospital until the end of his antibiotic course. 

# Multiple sclerosis: Currently, reports that Neuro exam is at 
baseline. Review of outpatient notes states that he has had 
difficulty eating. CXR did not show evidence of aspiration 
pneumonitis/pneumonia.  Per nursing, he was able to eat and take 
pills without any difficulty. He did, however, complain of a 
toothache (needs cavities filled) that prevented him from eating 
hard foods.  

#Dental pain: patient complained of a sore tooth in the R lower 
mandible and stated he needs cavities filled. He was unable to 
tolerate eating regular food because of the pain and loss of 
appetite and therefore received Ensures. He was evaluated by the 
dental service at ___ to ensure that no immediate management 
was required and he also received a CT head/neck and panorex. 
These imaging studies showed parotitis and cavities requiring 
that several teeth be pulled, but this was deemed appropriate 
for outpatient management. Per above, he was discharged on 
clindamycin and has dental follow-up scheduled at ___. A CD 
was made of his imaging studies and was sent with the patient.

# HLD: Stable  
- Continued home Zetia  
- Continued home aspirin 81 daily  

# Med Rec:  
- Continued home MVI, ascorbic acid, Zinc supplementation  
  
# Code: presumed full

EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/ CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with sepsis, dental carries and right mandibluar
tenderness. Evaluate for an abscess.

TECHNIQUE:  Head CT was obtained after intravenous contrast administration. 
DLP 890 cell mGy cm.

COMPARISON:  Noncontrast head CT ___.

FINDINGS: 

Evaluation for intracranial blood products is limited in the absence of a
precontrast scan.There is no evidence for pathologic intra-axial or
extra-axial contrast enhancement. There is no evidence for edema or mass
effect in the brain parenchyma. Foci of low density in the periventricular,
deep, and subcortical white matter of the cerebral hemispheres, similar to the
prior CT, are likely sequela of chronic small vessel ischemic disease in a
patient of this age.The ventricles and sulci are normal in size for age.

The bones are unremarkable. The imaged paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells
are well aerated.  Concurrent neck CT is reported separately.

IMPRESSION:

sensitive for intracranial infection, if clinically warranted.

EXAMINATION:  CT NECK W/CONTRAST (EG:PAROTIDS)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with sepsis, dental caries and right mandibluar
tenderness. Evaluate for an abscess.

TECHNIQUE:  Routine enhanced CT study of the neck was performed with images
obtained from the skull base to the thoracic inlet. Sagittal and coronal
reconstructions were performed.

DOSE:  DLP: 302 mGy-cm; CTDI:  9.54 mGy

COMPARISON:  None. Concurrent head CT with intravenous contrast an noncontrast
head CT from ___ are available for correlation.

FINDINGS: 

There is mild mucosal thickening along the floor of the right maxillary sinus.
There is no evidence for periapical lucencies in the maxilla.  There is caries
involving the left maxillary canine, first premolar and second premolar.

There is caries involving the left mandibular first premolar. There is a
periapical lucency involving the left maxillary first premolar, 2:53 and
602b:49, without cortical erosion or periosteal reaction. There is no evidence
for fluid collection in the adjacent soft tissues.

Right mandibular third molar is undescended. There is caries involving the
right mandibular canine and second premolar; the first right mandibular
premolar appears absent. There is a small periapical lucency along the right
mandibular second premolar, best seen on image 602b:36, which is adjacent to
the alveolar nerve canal. There is no evidence for associated cortical erosion
or periosteal reaction. There is no fluid collection in the adjacent soft
tissues.

There is mild subcutaneous edema in the right side of the face. Right parotid
gland appears enlarged with diffuse hyper enhancement, compatible with
parotitis. No associated stone is seen. Surrounding fat stranding. Extends to
the level of the right submandibular gland, which demonstrates enlargement and
heterogenous enhancement, without evidence for a stone. Right
sternocleidomastoid muscle is mildly thickened. Asymmetrically prominent right
level 2 and level 3 lymph nodes are likely reactive. There is no associated
rim enhancing fluid collection. However, there is diffuse retropharyngeal
fluid measuring up to 5 mm in maximal thickness, image 602b:36.

There is no evidence for an exophytic mucosal mass. No focal thyroid lesion is
detected, but evaluation by CTs limited compared to sonography.

Visualized upper lungs appear on unremarkable. There is no lymphadenopathy in
the visualized upper mediastinum.

There is evidence of ACDF from C5 through C7. This exam is not technically
optimized for detecting hardware loosening, but none is seen. There is minimal
retrolisthesis of C4 on C5. No suspicious lytic or sclerotic bone lesions are
seen.

Concurrent head CT is reported separately.

IMPRESSION:


1. Enlargement and hyper enhancement of the right parotid gland, consistent
with parotitis.  Enlargement and heterogenous enhancement of the right
submandibular gland, consistent with inflammation/infection as well.  No
evidence for an abscess.
2. Right cervical lymphadenopathy is likely reactive. Thickening of the right
sternocleidomastoid muscle is also likely reactive.
3. Diffuse retropharyngeal fluid without rim enhancement, a nonspecific
finding.
4. Multi focal dental caries. Periapical lucencies involving the left
maxillary first premolar and right mandibular second premolar, the latter
adjacent to the alveolar nerve canal, which may represent periapical abscesses
or sequela of prior periapical infections. Please correlate with dental exam.
No evidence for cortical erosion in the mandible or maxilla, and no evidence
for would collection in the buccal or lingual soft tissues of the mandible or
maxilla.

INDICATION:  Urinary tract infection needing antibiotics by a PICC.

COMPARISON:
Chest radiograph ___.

TECHNIQUE:
OPERATORS: Dr. ___, Interventional Radiology Fellow and Radiology
resident and Dr. ___ radiologist performed the proecdure. Dr.
___ supervised the trainee during the key components of the
procedure and has reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: 1% lidocaine was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues
overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: None.
CONTRAST: 0 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  2.8 min, 7 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Single lumen PICC placement through the brachial vein on the left.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia multiple
attempts were made to access the right brachial and basilic veins.  An attempt
to access the left brachial vein result in minor injury to the brachial
artery. And a pressure was held for hemostasis and ultrasound was repeatedly
performed, which showed a non expanding hematoma.

The left brachial vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Permanent ultrasound images were obtained before and after
intravenous access, which confirmed vein patency. A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire. The guidewire was then advanced into the superior
vena cava using fluoroscopic guidance. A single lumen PIC line measuring 42 cm
in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned
in the distal SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was
confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest. The peel-away sheath and
guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured to the skin, flushed,
and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  The accessed vein was patent and compressible.
2.  Brachialvein approach single lumen left PICC with tip in the distal SVC.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a left 42 cm brachial approach single lumen PowerPICC
with tip in the distal SVC.  The line is ready to use.

RECOMMENDATION:
 The findings were discussed by Dr. ___ with Dr. ___ telephone on
___ at 15:05.
